target.title: fix(outbound): message tool reports success while best-effort delivery failed
target.body:
Related: #84232

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents using the `message` tool to reply in the current conversation would see a normal, success-shaped result even when channel delivery actually failed or partially failed.

For channels that deliver agent replies through the message tool (`message_tool_only` mode — Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Telegram, and others), implicit current-source replies are forced to best-effort sends (#84232). In that mode `sendMessage()` discards the durable batch send outcome: a total delivery failure returns an envelope with no failure signal at all, and a partial failure (for example chunk 2 of 3 rejected) returns the last successfully delivered chunk's `messageId` — indistinguishable from a fully successful send. The agent believes the reply reached the user and keeps acting on that assumption.

The safety net that is supposed to catch this already exists: `deliveryEnvelopeIndicatesPartialDelivery` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.ts` checks tool result envelopes for `deliveryStatus: "partial_failed"` / `sentBeforeError`. But this send path never emitted those fields, so the detector could never fire.

## Why This Change Was Made

`MessageSendResult.deliveryStatus` is widened from only `"suppressed"` to `"sent" | "suppressed" | "partial_failed" | "failed"`, and the direct-send return in `sendMessage()` now populates it from the durable batch send result, together with a formatted `error`, `sentBeforeError`, and serialized per-payload `payloadOutcomes`. The derivation mirrors `deliveryStatusFromDurableSend` in `src/agents/command/delivery.ts`, which already projects the same durable send result honestly for agent command replies.

Throw semantics are intentionally unchanged: best-effort sends still resolve instead of throwing (the #84232 contract), and non-best-effort failures still throw. This change only makes the resolved envelope tell the truth. Non-goals: the best-effort policy itself, the partial-delivery detector, and the result shapes of the gateway-relayed and dry-run branches are untouched.

## User Impact

Agents (and anything else consuming message tool send results) can now distinguish a delivered reply from a dropped or partially delivered one. The already-shipped partial-delivery detection in the source-reply flow becomes effective for this path, so a failed visible reply is no longer silently treated as delivered. Successful sends now also carry an explicit `deliveryStatus: "sent"`; existing fields are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real-runtime capture (`node --import tsx`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, no mocks — the bundled Telegram plugin makes a real HTTPS call to `api.telegram.org` with an invalid bot token, so the send genuinely fails at the platform boundary with `401: Unauthorized`).

Before this change — the channel logs `message failed: Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (401: Unauthorized)`, yet the agent-visible envelope is success-shaped:

```json
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "to": "123456789",
  "via": "direct",
  "mediaUrl": null
}
```

After this change — same real 401, same call, envelope now reports the failure:

```json
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "to": "123456789",
  "via": "direct",
  "mediaUrl": null,
  "deliveryStatus": "failed",
  "error": "Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (401: Unauthorized)",
  "payloadOutcomes": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "status": "failed",
      "error": "Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (401: Unauthorized)",
      "sentBeforeError": false,
      "stage": "platform_send"
    }
  ]
}
```

Focused tests in `src/infra/outbound/message.test.ts` (all passing via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/message.test.ts`), written failing-first against the old behavior:

- best-effort total failure: still does not throw, now carries `deliveryStatus: "failed"` plus `error` and the failed payload outcome (previously indistinguishable from success)
- best-effort partial failure with one of two payloads sent: `deliveryStatus: "partial_failed"`, `sentBeforeError: true`, per-payload outcomes, `result` still the last delivered chunk
- regression: plain success reports `deliveryStatus: "sent"`; suppressed sends keep `deliveryStatus: "suppressed"`

Typecheck (`pnpm tsgo`), lint/format on the touched files, and the adjacent `src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.core-send.test.ts` suite also pass locally. Running the entire `src/infra/outbound/` test directory in one process is flaky on the local dev machine independent of this change (the same files fail on an unmodified checkout of the merge-base commit, with different failure sets across runs; each file passes when run on its own) — broad verification is deferred to CI.
